findings.title: Comment says resuming wakes the parent, but already-armed subagents of a settled parent still resume
findings.body: The new `NOT EXISTS` sits only inside the second (arm) branch of the OR. The first branch (lines 3958-3967) still returns an already-armed child once its reset passes, and `limitRecoveryCommand` then emits `message.dispatch` (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:63-78). The test at ProjectionStore.test.ts:5601 asserts this on purpose, so a subagent armed before its parent settled still starts a run at reset. The comment's reason, 'resuming it would wake the parent', applies to that path too. Is it intended that only fresh arming is blocked? If so, narrow the comment to say so. If not, the filter belongs on the resume branch as well.

contracts.action: Limit-recovery candidate query now excludes fresh arming for subagent threads whose parent has settledOverride = 'settled'
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing `settledOverride IS NOT 'settled'` check on the thread itself (line 3953), and the matching client-side check in limitRecoveryCommand (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:29).
contracts.before_after: Before: any failed usage-limit thread was an arm candidate, so a subagent of a settled parent got armed and later resumed. After: such a child is dropped from the arm branch. A child already armed for the same run and reset still goes through the first branch unchanged. The worker's `limitRecoveryCommand` (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:23-62) never checks the parent, so the SQL is the only guard.
contracts.visible_effect: Subagents of settled parents are no longer auto-resumed and no longer wake the parent. This affects only candidates that have not yet been armed.
contracts.failure_mode: If the parent settles after arming, the child still resumes at reset (see finding). The query is read-only, so the sweep logic does not change. The parent lookup is a per-row subquery run only for rows that reach the arm branch.

summary: The SQL change is small and correct for the arm path. The new test would fail on the parent commit, and it covers both the autoResume and snooze-only modes. It also pins the already-armed resume path. One open question: the guard stops fresh arming only, while the comment's reason ('resuming it would wake the parent') also holds for a child armed before its parent settled.
